title: Tiered-region-eviction-and-rollback-protocol + customer-bridge for cross-region KV desync
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Summary: A reproducible class of incidents has emerged where asymmetric leader leases during incremental region resynchronization lead to KV cache desynchronization and amplified tail latency for a subset of tenants. This ticket captures a new, tiered eviction-and-rollback protocol designed to: 1) stop customer-facing errors quickly with minimal traffic loss, 2) provide a safe surgical rollback path for affected region state, and 3) create a short customer bridge communication pattern for Hosted and Dedicated customers while the state patch is deployed.
mitigation_actions: Step 0: Activate emergency incident bridge (SRE + PM + ENG + CSM) and pin public comms template.
Step 1: Reduce region ALB weights to 0.2 and enable tenant-priority routing so only P0/P1 tenants keep sessions on the degraded region.
Step 2: Enable read-through KV fallback (cold read from cross-region authoritative snapshot) for affected shards to avoid stale in-memory responses.
Step 3: Temporarily disable continuous prefix caching for write-heavy tenants to prevent amplification of desync windows.
Step 4: Run cross-region KV quick-reconcile tool (dry-run) against a staging slice, then apply to production shards in a controlled order (low-first).
rollback_plan: If the reconcile patch causes increased 5xxs or latency > 2x baseline on canary pool, immediately revert orchestration change and re-enable prior routing weights. Use tenant snapshot restore for up to 1 hour of reconciliation; escalate to full region drain only if corruption is detected.
validation_checks: Synthetic end-to-end checks for tenant read/write consistency (green for 15m before proceeding)
Token-level tail-latency SLO check (p95/p99) against pre-incident baseline
KV checksum convergence metric (must show monotonic approaching zero divergence for 3 consecutive 5m windows)
communications: Internal: Start 30m rotating incident bridge with minutes published to #incident-channel and Slack 'incidents' roster.

Customer-facing: Two-tier bullet: (A) Immediate notification to affected Dedicated accounts with actions we are taking and ETA; (B) Hosted status page banner with link to detailed postmortem. Draft in docs: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-KV-comms
Support runbook: CSMs to use canned responses with escalation code 'REGION-KV-2026' and link to interim mitigation instructions for SDK retries.
postmortem_tasks: Create a detailed timeline (10s granularity) for state transitions during the incident
Add unit/integration tests for leader lease edge-cases that previously allowed phantoms
Instrument and dashboard the KV divergence metric with alert thresholds and runbook link
Customer follow-ups: 1:1 calls with top-10 affected Dedicated customers and credits review
progress_updates: 2026-03-08: Triage: observed repeated KV checksum divergence between us-east-1a and eu-west-1b during incremental rolling upgrade. Created this ticket to formalize protocol.
2026-03-09: SRE implemented temporary read-through fallback; immediate 40% reduction in 5xxs for affected tenants. Noted increased cold-read latency for some queries.
2026-03-11: Orchestration team produced a reconcile dry-run; canary on synthetic pool passed 30m validation. Prep for production patch scheduled.
2026-03-13: First production reconcile applied to low-priority shard group; observed checksum convergence and p99 latency stable. Beginning tier-2 canary early morning 2026-03-14.
comments: PM feedback (Jordan Lee): Ensure customer comms include concrete ETA and what to expect for Dedicated vs Hosted — customers need clarity on when traffic will move and if connections will be broken.
Design note (Rina Patel): Console should show 'region health' at tenant level during runbook steps; adding a temporary flag to surface in the console's tenant detail page.
Security review (TBD): need KMS approval if snapshot restore touches encrypted at-rest keys — pre-approval requested from Security on 2026-03-12.
notes: This protocol is intentionally conservative for Dedicated customers who require stronger isolation; default behavior differs between Hosted and Dedicated in the orchestrator config.
We will pair this ticket with a smaller follow-up that automates tenant-priority routing as an engine-level policy (ENG-714999).
Consider exposing a 'graceful-evict' API for enterprise customers to opt into controlled session handoff during region maintenance.
